title: Teaching a new cleaner: the training sequence
moduleTitle: Shared: Growing and managing a team
audience: Supervisors, trainers and senior cleaners who teach new workers a set of housekeeping or janitorial tasks.
learningOutcomes: Sequence a new worker's training from classroom content to supervised practice to final evaluation.
Use a demonstrate, watch, do and repeat cycle for each task.
Write a final evaluation that states what was achieved and what needs repeating.

instruction.heading: The order of training
instruction.body: The sample firm teaches theory before any on-the-job work, so trainees learn the basic knowledge and skills before they begin. New recruits are introduced to their section by the supervisor, taken through key company policies, and then gathered for a larger, organised training once they know the section's operations. The first organised training covers the specific standards and procedures for each type of site, the equipment used and the detergents needed.

instruction.heading: Demonstrate, watch, do and repeat
instruction.body: On the job the trainer first does the task while the trainee watches, then the trainee does a specific part of the task alone under observation. The sample stresses that a trainee who has not picked up the task should be taken through it again until it is fully understood. Move between sites when a task differs, for example from a rooms-based housekeeping task to an office-based janitorial one, so the trainee sees how the methods change.

instruction.heading: Supervised work and evaluation
instruction.body: After training, the new worker is given a permanent set of tasks and works under close supervision for the opening days. The sectional supervisor keeps the trainee in the assigned area and checks the work. A trainer then walks the work as a field supervisor and completes a final evaluation. The evaluation is passed to the manager responsible for training, who decides whether the training was effective. Keep the evaluation separate from the induction record, which is covered by “Staff onboarding and induction record”.

procedure: Introduce the trainee to the section, the key policies and the site rules.
Deliver the theory session on the standard procedures and the equipment used.
For each task, demonstrate it while the trainee watches, then have the trainee do the part they can manage with a check.
Repeat any task the trainee has not completed to standard, and record the repeat.
Supervise the opening days' work closely and note what was done correctly and what was not.
Complete the final evaluation and send it to the manager responsible for training.

workedExamples.situation: A new housekeeper is learning bed making and bathroom cleaning for short-stay rooms. The trainee completes the bed making but misses the bathroom grout on the first attempt.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the trainer do next, and what should the final evaluation say about the bathroom task?
workedExamples.reasoning: The trainer demonstrates the grout step again, watches the trainee repeat it, and records the repeat. The evaluation states that bed making was achieved, and that bathroom grout required a repeat and was re-checked on a later shift.

equipmentAndPpe: Task checklist, the product instructions for any product used, and standard PPE for the site.

commonErrors.error: Treating theory as enough and skipping the watched practice.
commonErrors.prevention: Follow the sequence: theory, watch, do, repeat.

commonErrors.error: Letting a trainee stay on a task they have not achieved.
commonErrors.prevention: Repeat the task and re-check it before moving on.

commonErrors.error: Writing a final evaluation that says the trainee is fully trained after one session.
commonErrors.prevention: Record what was observed, on which dates, and what remains to be checked.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Completing training does not grant a licence or any authority to do regulated work. Where a task needs one, the licence must be checked separately.
The sample's training duties were written for a non-Australian operation.

qualityStandard: Every task in the induction plan has a demonstration, a watched attempt and a recorded check.
The final evaluation lists achieved and repeated tasks with dates.
documentationEvidence: Training plan with tasks and dates.
Final evaluation report sent to the person who manages training.
summary: Training runs in order: theory, demonstration, watched practice, repeat, supervised work, evaluation.
A task is not signed off until it is achieved to standard and re-checked.
Completing training does not grant a licence or authority.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which sequence does the sample firm use for training?
options: Supervised work, then theory, then demonstration and then a short written quiz at the end
Evaluation first, then theory and then supervised work with a checklist and a quick test
Supervised work only, with no demonstration or practice first and then a short test on the day
Theory first, then on-the-job demonstration and watched practice, then supervised work and evaluation

knowledgeChecks.question: A trainee does not yet pick up a task. What should the trainer do?
options: Repeat the training until the task is fully understood, then re-check it
Sign the task off anyway and move on to the next task today
Take the trainee off the task for the rest of the month and give them a new task
Stop the training and move the trainee to a different task

knowledgeChecks.question: Which statement about a final training evaluation is accurate?
options: It proves the trainee is licensed and it lists the licence number
It records what was observed and what still needs repeating
It replaces all supervision for the rest of the year
It is only needed when a client complains and then filed away
